summary: Colorado treats a contractor building or repairing real property as the consumer of materials under a lump-sum contract, so the owner is charged no sales tax; under a time-and-materials contract the contractor collects tax on the separately stated materials only.

conditions.when: Lump-sum contract (one price; materials not stated separately from labor)
Time-and-materials contract: the separately stated, marked-up price of the construction materials
Time-and-materials contract: the separately stated labor

Not a building contract: an over-the-counter sale of a complete unit not made to order (an appliance, stock carpet, ready-made cabinets, storm doors and similar items) with an agreement to install it, the installation not segregated on the bid or invoice
Not a building contract: an over-the-counter sale of a complete unit not made to order with an agreement to install it: the installation charge, segregated on the bid or invoice

citations.title: 1 CCR 201-5, Colorado Sales and Use Tax Special Rules, Special Rule 10. Contractors
citations.quote: An over-the-counter sale of a complete unit not made to order, with an agreement for installation of the unit, is not a building contract.

citations.title: 1 CCR 201-5, Colorado Sales and Use Tax Special Rules, Special Rule 10. Contractors
citations.quote: On such sales the sales tax must be collected from the purchaser by the retailer-contractor. If the installation charges are segregated in the bid proposal or sales invoices, these charges are not taxable.

citations.title: FYI Sales 6, Contractors and Retailer-Contractors (03/20)
citations.quote: For lump-sum contracts, the contractor is treated as the consumer of all construction and building materials included in and associated with the contract.

citations.title: FYI Sales 6 (03/20)
citations.quote: The contractor does not collect any sales tax from the homeowner.

citations.title: FYI Sales 6 (03/20)
citations.quote: Instead, the contractor must collect sales tax from its customer on the marked up price of the materials included in the time-and-materials contract and remit the collected tax to the Department of Revenue.

citations.title: FYI Sales 6 (03/20)
citations.quote: The contractor does not collect sales tax from the homeowner on the price of labor stated in the time-andmaterials contract.

citations.title: FYI Sales 6 (03/20), who is a contractor
citations.quote: anyone engaged, under a contractual arrangement, in the construction, reconstruction, or repair of any building, bridge or structure; and

citations.title: FYI Sales 6 (01/12)
citations.quote: license and charge applicable taxes on the marked up billing price of all materials.

citations.title: FYI Sales 6 (01/12)
citations.quote: All supplies and materials are taxable on the contractor's cost, either through sales tax paid to the vendor or use tax paid by the contractor on the Consumer Use Tax Return (DR 0252).

notes: Covers both subcodes; Colorado draws no line between improvement and repair. 2012-01-01 is the date of the earlier FYI Sales 6 edition (01/12, archived 2016), which states the same split. Non-building materials (items that stay personal property) sold and installed by a contractor are retail sales. Local use taxes on building materials are often collected through building permits (C.R.S. 29-2-105(2)); home-rule cities administer their own contractor rules. 2026-11-02: the over-the-counter complete-unit cases are Special Rule 10 as archived (current: its notes record SR-5's repeal effective 10/30/2025); the editor's notes list every amendment from 03/01/2010 on and none to Special Rule 10, so its text has been in force since before this rule's 2012-01-01 start.

summary: A delivery charge for goods exempt from Colorado state sales tax is not taxable: it is either part of the exempt price or a separate, untaxed service.

citations.title: Colorado Sales Tax Guide (Oct 2025), Part 2
citations.quote: Sales of services are generally not subject to Colorado sales tax.

notes: This rule is the state part; local parts are in the CO:local rule (groceries may be taxable locally). Home-rule cities that collect their own sales tax (Denver, Aurora, Boulder, Colorado Springs and others) set their own bases and are not covered by Department of Revenue guidance; their treatment of this code was not researched.

summary: A delivery charge on taxable goods is excluded from Colorado's taxable price only if it is separately stated and separable (the buyer could choose to pick up instead); otherwise it is taxed with the goods.

Delivery is not optional (the goods are only sold delivered), the charge is overstated to shift price, or it is not separately stated

Colorado's retail delivery fee (C.R.S. 43-4-218, from 2022-07-01) is a separate fee excluded from the purchase price, not sales tax. Home-rule cities that collect their own sales tax (Denver, Aurora, Boulder, Colorado Springs and others) set their own bases and are not covered by Department of Revenue guidance; their treatment of this code was not researched.

Home-rule cities that collect their own sales tax (Denver, Aurora, Boulder, Colorado Springs and others) set their own bases and are not covered by Department of Revenue guidance; their treatment of this code was not researched.

summary: Food for home consumption (groceries) is exempt from Colorado's 2.9% state sales tax.

citations.title: C.R.S. 39-26-707(1)(e) (2024)

summary: Retail sales of general tangible goods are subject to Colorado state sales tax and the state-administered city, county and special district sales taxes.

notes: Covers all seven subcodes. Tangible goods sold along with a service (e.g. furnishings an interior designer sells, printed advertising materials, software on physical media) can be taxable, and a bundled sale of goods and service may be taxable in full unless the service is separately stated and separable (Sales Tax Guide, Part 3). Mainframe computer access is taxable as a sale of tangible personal property, but does not include ASP-hosted software. Home-rule cities that collect their own sales tax (Denver, Aurora, Boulder, Colorado Springs and others) set their own bases and are not covered by Department of Revenue guidance; their treatment of this code was not researched.

summary: Prewritten software is taxable in Colorado only when sold prepackaged, under a tear-open license, on a physical medium; downloaded or load-and-leave software is not taxable.

Delivered electronically (download) or by load and leave (installed from media the buyer does not keep)
Licensed under a written agreement signed by licensor and licensee (not a tear-open license), even on physical media

citations.quote: "Tangible personal property", commencing July 1, 2012, shall include computer software if the computer software meets all of the following criteria:

citations.title: C.R.S. 39-26-102(15)(c)(I)(C) (2024)
citations.quote: (C) The computer software is delivered to the customer in a tangible medium. Computer software is not delivered to the customer in a tangible medium if it is provided through an application service provider, delivered by electronic computer software delivery, or transferred by load and leave computer software delivery.

citations.title: Sales & Use Tax Topics: Computer Software (rev. Feb 2021)
citations.quote: Colorado sales tax applies to a sale of computer software if all of the following conditions are met: (1) it is prepackaged for repeated sale or license; (2) its use is governed by a tear-open nonnegotiable license agreement; and (3) it is delivered in a physical medium such as a tape, disk, compact disc, or card.

summary: Software accessed remotely from an application service provider (SaaS) is not taxable tangible personal property under Colorado's state and state-administered local sales taxes.

citations.title: C.R.S. 39-26-102(15)(c)(I)(C) (2024)
citations.quote: (C) The computer software is delivered to the customer in a tangible medium. Computer software is not delivered to the customer in a tangible medium if it is provided through an application service provider, delivered by electronic computer software delivery, or transferred by load and leave computer software delivery.

citations.title: Sales & Use Tax Topics: Computer Software (rev. Feb 2021)
citations.quote: Computer software is not subject to sales tax if it is delivered to the purchaser through any of the following methods: (1) it is provided to the customer through an application service provider; (2) it is delivered to the customer by electronic computer software delivery; or (3) it is transferred to the customer by load and leave computer software delivery.

citations.title: 1 CCR 201-4, Rule 39-26-102(15)(2)(d) (current)
citations.quote: computer software that does not meet the criteria enumerated in section 39-26-102(15)(c), C.R.S.

summary: Clothing, footwear, accessories and protective or sport equipment are taxable under Colorado state sales tax and state-administered local sales taxes.

citations.title: Colorado DOR Consumer Use Tax (archived November 27, 2020)
citations.quote: Examples of taxable products (often referred to as "goods") are electronics, appliances, furniture, home accessories, jewelry/watches, clothing, shoes, sports equipment or any other tangible personal property.

citations.title: Colorado DOR Sales Tax Guide, Part 2 (archived October 28, 2026)
citations.quote: Colorado imposes a sales tax on retail sales of tangible personal property except when such sales qualify for an exemption specifically authorized by law.

citations.title: C.R.S. 29-2-105(1)(d)(I), 2024
citations.quote: is the same as the sale of tangible personal property and services taxable pursuant to section 39-26-104, except as otherwise provided in this subsection (1)(d).

notes: Earliest checked dated clothing-specific evidence is the November 27, 2020 capture of the DOR consumer-use-tax page; its taxable-products list explains purchases for which sales tax was not collected. The later archived Sales Tax Guide confirms retail taxation. No clothing-specific exemption or threshold was found. State-administered local taxes follow the state base. Independently administered home-rule cities are excluded from this research, following the existing CO goods.general scope.
